rationale: The validation report explicitly flags issue=golden_rejected: the golden solution fails FR3 and SR1 because evaluate.py's register-extraction logic treats any secondary/contrastive mention of the non-primary register name (e.g. explaining why the other branch register is symmetrically exposed but not the one being reported) as ambiguous, even though the field clearly and primarily designates a single register as the answer. This is a false rejection caused by an overly brittle whole-word token-scan across the entire field text rather than checking which register is asserted as the primary/unambiguous answer. The golden submission is not at fault -- it correctly and thoroughly identifies the vulnerable register per FR3/SR1's ground truth; it simply also explains, for completeness, that the other register is symmetrically exposed. Per the golden_rejected rule, since the golden does not genuinely violate the spec, the fix belongs in evaluation_framework, not case_artifacts. Because the differential harness is blocked, mutation_score=0.0 is not meaningful and mapping/discrimination coverage cannot be trusted until this is fixed.
revision_instructions:
Rewrite the FR3 and SR1 checks in evaluate.py so they do not fail merely because both register names appear anywhere in the 'vulnerable_register' text. Implement a primary-register determination instead of a naive whole-text token scan: (1) identify the register name that is asserted as THE vulnerable register in the leading/primary clause of the field (e.g., the first register name mentioned, or the register that is the grammatical subject of an unqualified assertion such as 'X is the unverified branch register'); (2) treat any subsequent mention of the other register name as non-disqualifying if it appears within a clearly contrastive/explanatory clause (signaled by words like 'note', 'also', 'similarly', 'symmetrically', 'in contrast', 'unlike', or preceded by a sentence boundary that already completed the primary assertion) rather than being asserted with equal or ambiguous certainty as the answer; (3) only fail FR3/SR1 if the text asserts BOTH registers as candidates without designating one as primary (e.g., phrasing like 'either X or Q could be the vulnerable register' or lists them with no distinguishing primary claim). Grade this behaviorally against the field's semantic content, not by rejecting any text that contains both identifiers. Cross-check SR1 consistency by confirming the same primary register name also appears in trigger_scenario, per the existing consistency requirement. Add a regression fixture using the shipped golden answer file to CI so this check is exercised going forward. After patching, re-run the full differential validation (golden vs baseline vs mutants) to confirm the golden submission passes all 8 requirements end-to-end and that mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score rise above zero.
